executions.code:
# One-sample t-test power calculation
# H0: μ ≤ 0 vs H1: μ > 0 (one-sided, upper tail)
# Parameters:
# - Sample size: 25 participants
# - Mean difference to detect: 0.2 units
# - Standard deviation: 0.5 units
# - Significance level: 0.05 (one-sided)

library(stats)

n <- 25
delta <- 0.2  # Mean difference to detect
sd <- 0.5     # Standard deviation
alpha <- 0.05 # Significance level (one-sided)

# Calculate standardized effect size (Cohen's d)
d <- delta / sd
cat("Cohen's d (standardized effect size):", d, "\n")

# For a one-sample t-test, the noncentrality parameter is:
# λ = (mean_difference / sd) * sqrt(n)
lambda <- (delta / sd) * sqrt(n)
cat("Noncentrality parameter (λ):", lambda, "\n")

# Critical value for one-sided test at alpha = 0.05
df <- n - 1
critical_t <- qt(p = 1 - alpha, df = df)
cat("Critical t-value (df =", df, "):", critical_t, "\n")

# Power is the probability that the test statistic exceeds the critical value
# under the alternative hypothesis (non-central t distribution)
power <- 1 - pt(critical_t, df = df, ncp = lambda)
cat("Power:", power, "\n")

# Return result
result <- list(
  power = round(power, 15),
  n = n,
  delta = delta,
  sd = sd,
  alpha = alpha,
  d = d,
  lambda = lambda,
  critical_t = critical_t,
  df = df
)

cat("\n--- Summary ---\n")
cat("Power (decimal):", result$power, "\n")

library(jsonlite)

# Verification using alternative approach
n <- 25
delta <- 0.2
sd <- 0.5
alpha <- 0.05

# Method 1: Using non-central t distribution (as above)
df <- n - 1
lambda <- (delta / sd) * sqrt(n)
critical_t <- qt(p = 1 - alpha, df = df)
power_method1 <- 1 - pt(critical_t, df = df, ncp = lambda)

# Method 2: Using power.t.test from base R (verification)
# power.t.test doesn't directly give power for alternative hypothesis,
# so we use it to cross-check our delta parameter
power_verification <- power.t.test(
  n = n, 
  delta = delta, 
  sd = sd, 
  sig.level = alpha,
  type = "one.sample",
  alternative = "one.sided"
)

cat("Method 1 (Non-central t): Power =", power_method1, "\n")
cat("Method 2 (power.t.test verification):\n")
print(power_verification)

# Final result
power_final <- power_method1

# Emit structured JSON result
result_json <- list(
  results = list(
    list(
      metric = "power",
      value = round(power_final, 15),
      unit = "probability"
    )
  )
)

cat("\nPOWER_AGENT_RESULT=", toJSON(result_json, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15), "\n", sep = "")
